title: Suikoden III
subtitle: A conflict seen from three sides
summary: Suikoden III is Konami's PlayStation 2 role-playing game, first released in Japan on 11 July 2002. Its story follows three protagonists connected to the tensions between the Grasslands, Zexen and Harmonia. Hugo belongs to a Grassland clan, Chris Lightfellow commands Zexen knights and Geddoe serves with a Harmonian frontier force. Moving between them gives the same conflict different meanings. The player learns about the people on each side before their paths converge, making the growth of a shared cause depend on understanding how those separate journeys began.
body: Suikoden III is Konami's PlayStation 2 role-playing game, first released in Japan on 11 July 2002. Its story follows three protagonists connected to the tensions between the Grasslands, Zexen and Harmonia. Hugo belongs to a Grassland clan, Chris Lightfellow commands Zexen knights and Geddoe serves with a Harmonian frontier force. Moving between them gives the same conflict different meanings. The player learns about the people on each side before their paths converge, making the growth of a shared cause depend on understanding how those separate journeys began.

The Trinity Sight System divides the opening story between its principal viewpoints. Events experienced with one character gain another context when encountered through somebody else, so knowledge grows across the separate chapters. The player also recruits the series' Stars of Destiny, bringing a large cast into the developing alliance. These companions make the wider conflict tangible through individual meetings and tasks. A political situation that first appears as opposing groups gradually becomes a network of people who may be persuaded to help, each with a place in the campaign.

Suikoden III brought the series onto PlayStation 2 with three-dimensional characters and environments. Yoshitaka Murayama and Keiichi Isobe directed the project, while Michiru Yamane, Takashi Yoshida and Masahiko Kimura supplied the music. Its multiple protagonists distinguish it from the single central hero of the earlier games, giving the player a less settled view of the war. The Japanese and North American editions arrived in 2002. The game's defining choice remains its structure: before asking different people to fight together, it allows the player to spend time within their separate worlds.
